S_r ≡ (1/502) ∑_{t∈F_p^*} t^{-r}(1+t)^{10000} (mod p).

Change variables u = 1 + t to get
T_r = ∑_{u∈F_p, u≠1} u^{10000}(u−1)^{−r}
= ∑_{u∈F_p} u^{10000}(u−1)^{502−r}.

Expand (u−1)^{502−r} and use the power sum identity over F_p:
∑_{u∈F_p} u^k ≡ 0 unless k ≡ 0 mod (p−1), in which case the sum is −1 (mod p).

Write 10000 ≡ 462 (mod 502). The only contributing term in the expansion occurs when the exponent of u is 10000 + j ≡ 0 (mod 502), i.e., j ≡ 40 (mod 502). This term appears in the expansion only if 0 ≤ j = 40 ≤ 502 − r, i.e., iff r ≤ 462. Thus:
- If r ≥ 463, then T_r ≡ 0, hence S_r ≡ 0 (mod p).
- If r ≤ 462, then
  T_r ≡ −(−1)^{502−r−40} C(502−r, 40),
  so
  S_r ≡ (−1)^{462−r} C(502−r, 40) (mod p).

For 0 ≤ r ≤ 462, we have 40 ≤ 502 − r ≤ 502 < p, so C(502−r, 40) is nonzero modulo p (since all factors are less than p). Hence S_r ≠ 0 (mod p) for r ≤ 462.

Therefore, exactly those r with 463 ≤ r ≤ 501 give S_r ≡ 0 (mod 503). The count is 501 − 463 + 1 = 39.
